title: Corpus capabilities
description: The capabilities blob of CorpusRuntimeDiagnostics (Corpus.Capabilities): what an application can know before a run. It takes no manifest. Nodes run the same controller version as the host (the platform admits no other version to the work), so the stages, parsers and limits listed are the pool's. No node is named.

controller.description: The controller's version. The stages are built into the controller: one version, one stage set.

benchmark_unit.description: The unit of the pool's rate: megabytes of Common Crawl WET per second.

order.description: The stages in the order a document meets them. A manifest's pipeline switches turn extract_pdf, identify_language, clean_lines, filter_quality and sign on and off.

sha256.description: The stage set's fingerprint: the SHA-256 of the content hash the host computed for the controller's reference shard through the stages and of the PDF stage's contract (its module's pin, every limit and shaping rule), so a changed limit is a changed stage set.

verified.description: The fingerprint is the one the controller pins: the stages compute on the host what they compute everywhere.

language_format.description: The format of the language data the language stage reads (WITLID2, a language pack: profiles, acceptance limits and every language's rule data). It is a job's input pinned by language_model_sha256, so it is not in the fingerprint; WITLID1 models are still read.

html.description: The HTML parser behind the WARC text extraction, name and version.

compressor.description: The compressor of the text product, name, version and level.

language_model.description: A language model is a job's input (a blob, pinned by hash in the manifest), not part of the controller: a language pack (WITLID2) carries every language's profile, acceptance limit and rule data (script, stop words, thresholds), so adding a language is a new pack, not a new controller. The reference pack is the one the controller's tests and fleet proofs use.

format.description: The format of the reference pack (WITLID2, a language pack).

formats.description: Every model format the controller reads: WITLID1 (profiles only: the nearest profile always wins, the rule data is Corpus 0.1.14's, products as under 0.1.x) and WITLID2 (a language pack).

reference_sha256.description: What a manifest's pipeline.language_model_sha256 names to pin the reference pack.

reference_trained_from.description: The crawl the reference pack was built from.

reference_languages.description: ISO 639-3 codes of the languages the reference pack supports: what pipeline.target_languages may name with it.

reference_known_languages.description: ISO 639-3 codes of the languages the reference pack knows and does not support: a document in one of them is unknown and drops as unsupported_drop, not mislabelled.

witlid1_reference_sha256.description: The 0.1.x reference model (WITLID1), still read; a manifest pinned to it keeps its products.

unsupported_drop.description: The drop rule of a document in a language the pack does not support (language_unsupported).

unknown_drop.description: The drop rule of a document with too little text to tell its language (language_unknown).

formats.description: The source formats a manifest may name.

origins.description: Where a machine fetches from. A manifest's allowed_origins narrows this rule; it cannot widen it.

public.description: The public origins every machine fetches from: HTTPS, the default port, public addresses only.

machine_variable.description: The environment variable in which a machine's owner lists further hosts; only that machine fetches from them.

max_redirects.description: Redirect hops followed, each put to the same rule.

defaults.description: What applies when the options leave a value unset (0).

downloads_per_node.description: Shards a node downloads at once, whatever its degree.

memory_per_shard_bytes.description: Memory a node budgets per shard in flight; with its cores it bounds the node's degree.

ceilings.description: The most a job may ask for, and the limits a hostile input meets.

max_shard_bytes.description: A shard on the wire; the options can only lower it.

record_bytes.description: A larger WARC record is skipped and counted.

size_probes.description: Sources the server asks the origin for a size per preflight; the rest are estimated at the mean.

dedup_documents.description: Documents one Corpus.Dedup holds in memory.

pipeline.description: The stage parameters a manifest's pipeline may set, with the defaults that apply when it does not.

extract_pdf.description: The PDF stage on WARC shards (see pdf).

filter_curly_bracket.description: C4's curly-bracket rule, off unless the manifest turns it on.

output.description: pipeline.output: what a run keeps on the server. "full" keeps every shard's text and signatures; "stats_and_hashes" keeps the statistics, the content hashes, the report and the integrity document only (the text and the signatures stay on the node and are deleted with the task; no near-duplicate merge).

minhash.description: pipeline.minhash: the MinHash parameters of the signatures and the near-duplicate merge, with their defaults and ranges (0 or absent: the default). A signatures blob made with another hash count or shingle size than the defaults starts with WITSIG2 and states its shingle size; Corpus.Dedup refuses to merge signatures made with different parameters.

hashes.description: Hash functions per signature (8 bytes each, per document).

bands.description: LSH bands of the merge; must divide the hash count.

quality.description: pipeline.quality keys and their defaults: for scripts with word spacing and for those without (where a word is a letter). null: the rule does not apply to that kind of script.

quality_fixed.description: Thresholds of the quality filter that a manifest cannot set (yet).

top_ngram_chars.description: The most characters the single most frequent word n-gram may cover, n = 2, 3, 4.

duplicate_ngram_chars.description: The most characters repeated word n-grams may cover, n = 5 to 10.

pdf.description: The PDF stage (pipeline switch extract_pdf, WARC shards only): a response that is a PDF becomes text in the controller's own wasm sandbox, then page-range documents that go through the stages after it like a page of HTML. Every value here is part of the stage set's fingerprint.

formats.description: The shard formats that carry PDFs.

extractor.description: The extractor module: what it is built from.

module_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the extractor module; a module with other bytes is not run.

engine.description: The sandbox: the wasmtime binding the controller is built against.

available.description: Whether the host's process can run the stage. A node that cannot does not make the product of a shard that holds a PDF: the shard fails there as a fault of the node and runs on another; a shard without a PDF runs on it.

fuel.description: The fuel one PDF may burn, counted from the guest's _start.

fuel_after_instantiation.description: The budget is given after the module is instantiated, so it does not depend on the platform.

memory_bytes.description: The cap of the module's linear memory.

input_bytes.description: The largest PDF the stage runs.

text_bytes.description: The most text one PDF may give (more: pdf_oversized).

document_words.description: The most words of one page-range document; pages are put together while they fit, a longer page is a document of its own cut after the last line that fits.

document_id.description: How a page-range document is named in the product's url field.

running_lines.description: Running headers and footers: a line that, with each run of digits folded, appears on half the pages or more of a PDF of min_pages pages or more is removed from every page.

drops.description: The drop rules a PDF that gives no document is counted under.

signatures.description: The default MinHash parameters (pipeline.minhash sets others): the hashes, the shingle size, one document's signature in bytes, the merge's bands and rows per band.

bands.description: LSH bands of the dedup merge.

drop_rules.description: Every rule a shard's statistics can count a drop under, with the stage that applies it, in the order a document meets them: extract (records and PDFs that give no document), language, lines, quality. The report's funnel sums the drops by these stages.

per.description: One per shard execution, one per CorpusProcess job, or one per CorpusDedup run.

schema.description: The schema tag of a JSON document; "" for a product with a fixed binary or JSON-lines layout (the README).

outputs.description: The output modes that keep the product on the server.

storage.description: What the preflight's storage estimate is built on, and the room the deployment gives one job.

text_per_byte.description: Bytes of compressed text product per byte of shard fetched.

documents_per_mib.description: Documents in the product per MiB of shard fetched; each is one signature of signatures.bytes_per_document.

margin.description: What the largest measured value was raised by.

headroom_bytes.description: The most one job may leave on the server, as the deployment states it. Absent when it states none: storage then refuses nothing.

retention_days.description: Days the server keeps a job's products after they are made. Absent when the deployment does not say.

pool.description: The nodes that can take Corpus shards for this submitter now, as totals; absent when the host cannot say. No node is named.

measured.description: Nodes that have measured themselves on the reference shard; the next two numbers are theirs.

workers.description: Shards the measured nodes process at once, added up. Absent when the host does not carry the degree of every measured node.

rate.description: Megabytes of Common Crawl WET per second, added up.
